clue.text: Level with rower having limited sleep

indicators.note: the rower is pictured having, or holding, the short sleep inside him

parts.note: an oar is a person who rows as well as the blade itself
a nap is a short, limited spell of sleep

explanation.surface: A rower is barely keeping pace with his crew because he has had little sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: two things on equal terms or at the same standard are on a par, so level with each other.

clue.text: Order Diana to go to hospital department to be disciplined

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Di is the short form of the name Diana
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Diana is ordered to report to a hospital department for disciplinary action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well disciplined does as they are told, so is dutiful and compliant.

clue.text: Humming coming from a telephone call

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is informal for phoning them

explanation.surface: A humming noise is coming out of a phone during a call.
explanation.definitionFit: A place full of activity and excited noise is humming or alive with chatter.

clue.text: Leave a group of players performing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, or players
a performer currently on stage is said to be on

explanation.surface: A group of musicians leaves the stage mid-performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or walk away from something for good is a stronger synonym of leave.

clue.text: Fielding side strives for this kind of effort

definitions.text: Fielding side strives for this kind of effort

parts.words: Fielding side strives for this kind of effort
parts.note: in cricket the fielding team tries to dismiss every batsman, getting the batting side out completely; the phrase also means a maximum effort

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side bowls and catches, trying to dismiss all ten batsmen of the other team.
explanation.definitionFit: A total, no-holds-barred effort is described with the same phrase as a team being completely dismissed in cricket.

clue.text: Permit silence to be shattered

indicators.note: a thing shattered breaks into pieces, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grants permission for the quiet to be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to authorise or formally allow something is a synonym of permit.

clue.text: Band or artist's carrying case

parts.note: a chest is a large box or case for storage
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword shorthand for an artist

explanation.surface: A musical group, or perhaps a painter, lugging an instrument case about.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of instrumental musicians playing together is a kind of band.

clue.text: Attempt to limit ruin with it

indicators.note: the attempt bounds the ruin on both sides, holding it inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to end something can mean to ruin or finish it

explanation.surface: Trying to contain the damage with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it is slang for being fashionable and up to date, which this adjective also means.

clue.text: Ringmaster?

parts.note: not the circus compere but one who masters the boxing ring, a title-holding fighter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringmaster' suggests the circus, but the ring here is the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A title-holding prizefighter is master of the boxing ring, punning on the circus role.

clue.text: Leave willingly

parts.note: to leave something by will, in a testament, is to pass it on to an heir; willingly is read as by means of a will

explanation.walkthrough: 'Willingly' seems to mean gladly, but it is read as 'by will': leaving property in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing on possessions through a legal testament after death is the precise legal sense of this verb.

clue.text: Seen in court, a revolutionary quality that attracts admiration

indicators.note: the clue says the following pieces are seen inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary appears in court, displaying a charisma that wins admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige or distinction that makes something admired is what this borrowed French word names.

clue.text: Hiss: 'Turn over if snoring!'

indicators.note: turning over the little word if means reading its letters backwards

parts.note: ZZ is the comic-strip spelling of the sound of someone snoring

explanation.surface: Someone hissing at a snorer to roll over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissing sound of escaping gas or bubbles, as from a fizzy drink, is a synonym.

clue.text: Instruction to make less noise in bars

definitions.text: Instruction to make less noise in bars

parts.words: Instruction to make less noise in bars
parts.note: bars are measures of written music, not pubs, so this is a marking on a score telling players to grow gradually quieter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs and a call for quiet at closing time, but it means the bars of a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning a gradual decrease in volume, written into the score.

clue.text: Obstinate nine starting to waver

indicators.note: letters made to waver shift unsteadily into a new order

explanation.surface: A stubborn group of nine who are beginning to show doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubbornly refusing to change their views or compromise is described with this adjective, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Suggest about 100 correct to hold Queen's award

indicators.note: the first pieces are made to hold the award inside them

parts.note: re is Latin for 'about', as in memo headings
C is the Roman numeral for 100
to mend is to correct or put right
the OM, Order of Merit, is an honour in the monarch's personal gift

explanation.surface: Someone proposes about a hundred fitting nominees for a royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something forward as worth doing or choosing is to advise or propose it.

clue.text: Padre, with joy, reformed menace

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A priest, now joyful, has turned over a new leaf after being a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger or threat of harm is a sense shared with menace as a noun.

clue.text: Premier craftsman?

parts.note: a Prime Minister forms a government team, so a premier is one who assembles a cabinet; really a carpenter of fine furniture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' seems to mean top-quality, but it is the Prime Minister, who picks a cabinet of ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled woodworker who builds fine furniture such as cupboards, and whimsically a Prime Minister choosing ministers.

clue.text: Enthusiast having nothing on is a fool

parts.note: a buff is a keen fan, as in a film buff
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A fan with no clothes on makes a fool of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown or ridiculous person who behaves comically is a synonym.

clue.text: Small child with Terence has no right to be unsteady

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the name is left without one of its letters standing for right

parts.note: Terry is the usual short form of Terence

explanation.surface: A toddler and Terence are wobbly on their feet without support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has no right' removes one R from TERRY, leaving TERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and wobbly on one's feet, likely to stagger, means the same as unsteady.

clue.text: One cannot go straight ahead and make it

definitions.text: One cannot go straight ahead and make it

parts.words: One cannot go straight ahead and make it
parts.note: when the road ahead is closed, a driver has to take an indirect route around the obstacle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make it' seems to mean succeed, but it means taking a roundabout route.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout route taken when the direct way is blocked is exactly what one makes here.

clue.text: Top farmers cultivated polar ground

indicators.note: cultivated land is turned over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The best farmers have managed to grow crops on Arctic land.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil that stays frozen all year round in Arctic and Antarctic regions is this kind of ground.

clue.text: Cried quietly with rain around

indicators.note: the rain is placed around the musical sign for quiet

parts.note: the wet is a colloquial name for rainy weather
P, piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone shed tears silently while the rain fell around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of weep, meaning shed tears, is a straightforward synonym of cried.

clue.text: West Country lady

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A lady from the West Country, the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is the English south-west; here 'West' and 'Country' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A female adult, a synonym of lady in its general everyday sense.

clue.text: Spanish cheer during little brother's dance

indicators.note: the cheer comes in the middle of the brother, so it is placed within that word

parts.note: bro is a short, little, form of brother
olé is the Spanish shout of approval heard at bullfights

explanation.surface: Someone shouts olé while their kid brother performs a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish dance in triple time, also known from Ravel's famous orchestral piece.

clue.text: For always, nevertheless!

parts.note: the joke swaps never for its opposite ever, and less for its opposite more, turning the word nevertheless upside down in sense

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'nevertheless' into NEVER and LESS and replace each with its opposite to get the answer, which also means for always.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word meaning forever, for all time, as in the refrain of Poe's raven.

clue.text: Squirrel, perhaps not red, frisky

indicators.note: letters that are frisky jump about playfully into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A squirrel, possibly a grey one rather than red, running around playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel is one example of a gnawing mammal of this order, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Man that's found in New South Wales

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, as in the writer Sidney or the actor Poitier's spelling variant
the largest city in Australia lies in the state of New South Wales

explanation.surface: A man discovered living in an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name and also the state capital of New South Wales.
